_comment: Worked example of a marking ledger — the input to Resolve-MarkingLedger.ps1. Fictional students. Everything a marking run needs and nothing it can derive: no overall results, no dates other than the marking date, no filenames, no invoice flags. Those are computed, and stating them by hand is how a marking record ends up disagreeing with the SAR it summarises.
location: Meridian Vocational College, Training Kitchen 2, Adelaide
environment: Simulated environment — commercial training kitchen operating to industry service periods
_toolsComment: The tool names are the ACTUAL names on the assessment documents. They print as the two column headings on the marking record and as the tool rows on every SAR, so they must read the same in all three places — which they do, because they are written here once.

tools.name: Recipe Workbook and Observation of Direct Competency — Practical Demonstration

students._case: Straightforward Competent — and BOTH TOOLS IN ONE FILE. Mei submitted a single workbook covering the knowledge questions and the recipe workbook, so both results name the same 'evidence' path. The resolver groups them and she gets ONE marked copy, MARKED_MVC00312_SITHPAT016_kq-rw_02092026.docx, with every question marked through it and a declaration page naming both tools. Give them different paths and she would get two.

results._endAnchorComment: Her workbook does not end after Q12 — the recipe cards and the observation sheet follow it in the same file. So the knowledge questions stop at Part B, not at 'End of assessment'. Point it at the end of the document and Q12's outcome lands inside the observation sheet.
results.feedback: You answered all twelve knowledge questions and your explanations of gelatine ratios and of the three dessert sauce faults met the requirements of the unit. Your answer on storing sponge components covered temperature and covering. This assessment is satisfactory.

results._evidenceComment: The SAME file as the knowledge questions above. That is what makes this one marked copy rather than two.
observations: Observed mise en place complete before service.

results._sheetComment: The record is written INTO the observation sheet in her workbook: the four task boxes ticked, the date and times filled, the notes under the notes heading, the feedback on its own line and the sufficiency box ticked Yes. Everything is addressed by text the sheet actually carries.

results._questionsComment: EVERY question on the assessment carries an outcome, so every answer on the returned copy carries a green Satisfactory or a red Not yet Satisfactory. A question left out of this list is a question the student gets back with no remark on it.

items.action: Re-do the crème caramel and state aloud the colour you are checking for before you pour. Your assessor will observe this.
